description: Join us and let's create something fun and worth while.
summary:
**Artemis-0** is a first-person 3D lunar-habitat simulation and narrative survival game built in Godot 4.7 for learners aged 10–14. Players step into the boots of the first civilian volunteer at a lunar outpost, maintaining interconnected environmental control and life-support systems (ECLSS) while tracking a newly discovered deep-space object approaching Earth. NASA data feeds and CSA-inspired food-production mechanics connect the gameplay to real space science.

The game turns engineering trade-offs into consequential choices. Its hydrogen–oxygen fuel-cell model converts hydrogen and oxygen into water and electricity while drawing on limited gas reserves; water electrolysis can regenerate those gases but requires substantial power. Rehydrating food, running oxygen scrubbers, and calibrating the Deep-Space Network radar array all compete for finite energy, water, and supplies.

Artemis-0 addresses the challenge by making these interdependencies tangible rather than presenting them only as equations or technical text. It matters because it gives young learners an engaging way to explore closed-loop resource management—and how the same principles of efficiency and sustainability apply both in space and on Earth.
details:
**Artemis-0** is a first-person 3D lunar-outpost simulation and narrative survival game built in Godot 4.7 for learners aged 10–14. Players take the role of a civilian volunteer responsible for keeping the habitat operating while entering observations about a mysterious object approaching Earth. Story dialogue, a command-center interface, and a focused Science terminal connect the maintenance tasks to the unfolding narrative.

The game models interconnected environmental control and life-support systems. A fuel cell consumes hydrogen and oxygen to produce water and electrical energy in a 1:8:9 mass ratio; electrolysis can regenerate those gases from water, but requires substantial power. Players balance that loop against other demands, including oxygen scrubbing, food preparation, water use, and transmitting radar observations. A low-poly hydroponic grow rack and greenhouse mechanics introduce food production and water recovery, drawing inspiration from CSA lunar food-production research.

NASA data sources—including NeoWs, JPL Sentry, DONKI, and EPIC metadata—provide a real-world reference for asteroid records, impact-risk monitoring, space weather, and Earth-facing context. Live requests are on demand; bundled offline data and explicit unavailable messages help the prototype remain usable without a successful connection. The asteroid emergency and character story are fictional, not NASA predictions.

The project was developed with **Godot 4.7**, **GDScript**, **JSON**, and NASA’s public APIs. Procedural low-poly 3D construction and lightweight visuals were chosen with modest hardware in mind; performance on every target device has not been independently benchmarked.

Artemis-0’s creative approach is to make abstract systems tangible: each choice competes for limited energy, water, and gas, while data entry and maintenance carry narrative stakes. Design considerations included the intended young audience, readable interfaces, isolation and survival tone, resource interdependence, offline fallback behavior, and a clear distinction between verified science and fictional events. Its intended impact is to encourage learners to explore systems thinking, space science, and resource sustainability principles relevant to both space habitats and life on Earth.
